Strong emergence posits ontologically new causal powers; weak emergence accepts that higher-level patterns are in principle derivable but computationally intractable.

**Reductionism** insists all phenomena reduce to lower-level mechanisms. Nothing "truly new" appears; apparent emergence reflects incomplete analysis. Given sufficient computational power and initial conditions, higher-level behavior should be deducible from fundamental laws.

The architecture itself does explanatory workâ€”not by violating lower-level laws, but by determining which of countless micro-compatible states the system explores.

The productive view treats emergence and reduction as complementary tools, not metaphysical rivals. Different questions demand different grain sizes. Insisting every explanation drill down to quarks is as unproductive as mystifying higher-order patterns.
